item.title: Fluidization in Growth-Induced Morphogenesis
item.description: arXiv:2609.05858v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Elastic buckling has explained shape formation in growing tissues, yet the role of tissue fluidity remains elusive. We derive a minimal fluidized growth-elasticity model as a nonlinear analogue of Maxwell rheology. Analysis of a growing strip shows that fluidity promotes symmetry breaking under compression while regulating stress accumulation, so morphogenesis develops continuously before the elastic buckling threshold. Fluidity further controls the flow pattern, from smooth sinusoidal undulations to widened crests and localized indentations, with low fluidity favoring stronger localization.
item.dc:creator: Min Wu
